claim: The vLLM Router runs 'either in a K8s or a bare metal GPU cluster,' i.e. it is not architecturally tied to Kubernetes.
stance_target: routers can support non-K8s backends without abandoning vLLM-ecosystem tooling
scope_conditions: vLLM Router as of its Dec 2025 release announcement
quoted_support: Built in Rust for minimal overhead, the router acts as an intelligent, state-aware load balancer that sits between clients and a fleet of vLLM workers, either in a K8s or a bare metal GPU cluster.

claim: vLLM Router claims 25% higher request throughput and 1200ms faster TTFT than llm-d on Llama 3.1 8B with 8 prefill/8 decode pods, and throughput close to llm-d with 2000ms faster TTFT on DeepSeek V3 with 1 prefill (TP8) + 1 decode (TP8).
stance_target: llm-d's router/EPP is the highest-performance option for P/D-disaggregated serving
scope_conditions: vLLM's own internal benchmark, methodology and raw data not published; benchmarked against llm-d and a basic K8s-native round-robin LB
quoted_support: vLLM Router (blue line) Req/S throughput is 25% higher than llm-d (purple line) and 100% higher than K8s-native load balancer (orange line). vLLM Router’s TTFT is close to K8s-native load balancer and 1200 ms faster than llm-d.

claim: vLLM Router's benchmark excluded vLLM's own built-in DP/EP coordinator (the documented 'External Load Balancing' recommendation for vLLM clusters) because its throughput was only 1/8 of the others due to a known performance bug.
quoted_support: We excluded the vLLM built-in DP/EP coordinator—the recommended External Load Balancing solution for vLLM clusters—from the benchmark. Its throughput was only 1/8 of the others due to a known performance issue.

claim: The vLLM Router benchmark against llm-d was produced with direct input from llm-d engineers, not an independent third party.
scope_conditions: acknowledgements section of the vLLM Router announcement blog
quoted_support: Finally, we thank Tyler Michael Smith and Robert Shaw for sharing llm-d expertise and receipts which unblocked performance optimizations and benchmarks.

claim: The vLLM Router supports discovery for P/D disaggregation via NIXL and via NCCL-based transfer with ZMQ discovery, both of which are transport-level mechanisms independent of Kubernetes service discovery.
stance_target: non-K8s worker discovery mechanisms exist and are production-used
quoted_support: It supports discovery and routing for both NIXL and NCCL-based (with ZMQ discovery) disaggregation backends.
